slides.title: The spinner stall
slides.text: One Fairground stall runs a spinner with 6 equal parts, and only 1 part is red. Yesterday the stall keeper called red a sure thing. Tally spun it 30 times, and red landed just 4 times.

slides.title: Words for maybes
slides.text: Chance has its own words, and each one is a promise about the parts. Certain means every part, impossible means no part, and unlikely means a small share. This spinner gives red 1 part of 6.

visual.label: A spinner drawn as a bar cut into 6 equal parts, with 1 part shaded for red

focus.cue: One red part out of 6 equal parts.
Every other part is not red: 5 of the 6.
Six equal parts in all. Equal parts make the chance fair to judge.

slides.title: Worked example: sorting the words
slides.text: Rough first: the words should spread out, because the stalls are all different. Sort four stalls by their red parts: all red is certain, half an even chance, one of 6 unlikely, none impossible.
steps: 3 parts of 6 red: an even chance

visual.label: A strip of four chance-word tiles in order: certain, likely, unlikely, impossible

focus.cue: Certain: it happens every single time.
Unlikely: it can happen, but it probably will not.

slides.title: The Jumble calls it impossible
slides.text: The Jumble watched the spinner miss red five times and called red impossible. Then it landed on the very next spin. Unlikely things happen; that is what unlikely means. Impossible is a promise the parts can actually keep.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for maybes, in order.

words.means: how likely something is, judged from its share of the parts
it will probably happen, because most of the parts are its
it can happen, but probably will not, because few parts are its
it cannot happen, because no part is its

slides.title: Stretch: build a likely spinner
slides.text: Stretch: design a spinner where landing on red is likely but not certain. How many of its 8 parts are red, and why not all 8? Stretch work is never in the check.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather. It opens straight on the Numbers topic: play one whole run to its end card. Before each pick, say how sure you are: certain, likely, an even chance, unlikely or impossible. Then tally 20 real spins of any spinner and compare.
slides.alt: Would You Rather, the Numbers topic: a numbers choice on screen, two big cards to pick from, at the start of a run.
